paragraphs: Wigan Council has more than 230 fostering households of its own and says it most needs carers for older children, brothers and sisters who should stay together, and children with complex needs. Children from Wigan may also live with independent agencies such as those listed on this page.

The council pays a weekly allowance in tiers. From 6 April 2026 a newly approved carer looking after a child aged 5 to 10 receives £328.39 a week, rising to £414.20 at the experienced tier, with higher rates for older children and a specialist tier above that. Birthday, festival and holiday allowances, help with equipment and school uniform, and long-service bonuses are paid on top.

Becoming a carer usually takes about six months: an initial call, Skills to Foster training, checks including a medical and DBS, home assessment visits, then a fostering panel. Once approved, carers have a duty social worker, out-of-hours advice, support groups and mentoring, the Mockingbird peer support model, a counselling service, more than 200 training courses and discounted leisure membership.
Before deciding, compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about pay, training and support near you.
